title: Histological Structure and Cytomorphometric Characteristics of the Heart of the African Sharptooth Catfish (Clarias gariepinus)
content: Information on the tissue and cellular organization of the myocardium in the African sharptooth catfish (Clarias gariepinus) remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the histological structure of the atrial and ventricular myocardium, determine the relative proportions of its tissue components, and characterize the cytomorphometric parameters of cardiomyocytes. Hearts from sexually mature, clinically healthy fish (n = 10) were examined. Histological and morphometric methods were employed, and data from the ten fish were expressed as the mean ± standard error (Mean ± SE). Histological sections were stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The ventricular wall consisted of three layers: the epicardium, myocardium, and endocardium. The myocardium exhibited a well-developed trabecular architecture composed of multidirectionally oriented cardiomyocyte bundles separated by connective tissue. The thicknesses of small-, medium-, and large-caliber muscular bundles were 26.13 ± 3.02, 42.37 ± 1.30, and 63.07 ± 1.70 μm, respectively. The relative areas occupied by muscle fibers and connective tissue were 72.03 ± 1.14% and 28.60 ± 1.55%, respectively. Cardiomyocyte width ranged from 7.63 ± 0.46 to 12.90 ± 0.38 μm, depending on cell size, whereas the calculated nuclear volume ranged from 42.13 ± 1.74 to 66.90 ± 2.72 μm³. The atrial myocardium was thinner and formed a loosely organized network of interconnected muscular bundles. Cells with distinct morphological characteristics, including spindle-shaped cells and cells with vacuolated sarcoplasm, were observed in the atrial myocardium. These findings provide further insight into the myocardial histoarchitecture of C. gariepinus and may serve as a morphological basis for assessing adaptive and pathological changes under different rearing conditions.
